To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of human papiloma virus (HPV)-DNA in penile cancer (pSCC), independent of histological tumor grade, indicates a more indolent behavior.
p16INK4 expression is the best predictor for the presence of high-risk HPV DNA, but neither HPV status nor histologic grade correlates with the risk of nodal involvement or metastasis.
the p16INK4A status is a good predictor for the presence of HPV DNA in penile carcinoma and that HPV positivity and p16INKA4A expression are associated with a less aggressive local tumour behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the histologic subtype, the p16INK4 expression and the presence of human papiloma virus DNA in penile carcinoma.
the role of p16INKA4a expression and presence of human-papillomavirus DNA as a prognostic factor in patients with squamous-cell carcinoma of the penis.
HPV-associated pSCC and its prognostic relevance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HPV/p16INK4a detection in pSCC should be restricted to those tumours with an unclear histological subtype or to those with a basaloid subtype.
HPV testing in pSCC is not necessary in the setting of routine histopathology.
the presence of p16INKA4a in the nuclei of pSCC cells is a good indicator of HR-HPVs, which are associated with less aggressive tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPV-related pSCC is not more aggressive than HPV-unrelated tumours, and that the presence of HPV in the tumour is not an independent prognosticator.
pSCC patients with p16INK4-positive, HR-HPV-positive tumours may benefit from less aggressive local treatment.
the histopathologic diagnosis of pSCC should be based on the morphological appearance of tumour cells, and not the presence of p16INKa and/or HR-HPV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p16INK4 expression pattern in pSCC may be more important than the HPV status in determining the biological behavior of these tumors.

pSCC with intense nuclear staining for p16INKA4a is a good predictor for HR-HPV infection and a less aggressive local behavior, which may be helpful to select patients for organ-sparing treatment strategies.
the presence of HR- HPV DNA in penile cancer is not associated with a more aggressive disease.
